source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Keeps imprisonment, both senders and Philemon's two relations.
verses.before: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our beloved fellow worker,
verses.after: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our beloved coworker,
verses.tsw_comparator: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our beloved fellow worker,

verses.rationale: Preserves both names, gendered kinship, military metaphor and household church.
verses.before: to Apphia our sister, Archippus our fellow soldier, and the church in your house:
verses.after: to Apphia our sister, Archippus our fellow soldier and the church that meets in your house:
verses.tsw_comparator: and Apphia our sister, and Archippus our fellow soldier, and the church in your house:

verses.rationale: Keeps plural recipients and paired blessing.
verses.before: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.after: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated gratitude and prayer.
verses.before: I always thank my God when I mention you in my prayers,
verses.after: I always thank my God when I remember you in my prayers,
verses.tsw_comparator: I give thanks to my God always when I remember you in my prayers,

verses.rationale: Keeps the crossed relation of faith/love and their two objects.
verses.before: because I hear about your love and trust toward the Lord Jesus and for all the holy ones.
verses.after: because I hear of your love and faith toward the Lord Jesus and for all the saints.
verses.tsw_comparator: because I hear of your love and of the faith that you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all the saints,

verses.rationale: Retains partnership, efficacy and the difficult knowledge phrase.
verses.before: I pray that the sharing of your trust may become effective through the knowledge of every good thing among us for Christ.
verses.after: I pray that the sharing of your faith may become effective through recognizing every good thing among us for Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: and I pray that the sharing of your faith may become effective in the knowledge of every good thing that is in us for the sake of Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily-heart idiom, family address and prior refreshment.
verses.before: For I have received much joy and encouragement from your love, because the hearts of the holy ones have been refreshed through you, brother.
verses.after: For I have received great joy and encouragement from your love, brother, because through you the hearts of the saints have been refreshed.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have derived much joy and comfort from your love, my brother, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you.

verses.rationale: Preserves real authority and the command Paul could issue.
verses.before: Therefore, although I have great boldness in Christ to command you to do what is fitting,
verses.after: Therefore, though in Christ I have great boldness to command you to do what is fitting,
verses.tsw_comparator: Accordingly, though I am bold enough in Christ to command you to do what is required,

verses.rationale: Keeps appeal, age claim and imprisonment as persuasive pressure.
verses.before: because of love I prefer to appeal to you—being such a person as Paul, an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
verses.after: I prefer to appeal to you on the basis of love—being who I am, Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet for love’s sake I prefer to appeal to you—I, Paul, an old man and now a prisoner also for Christ Jesus—

verses.rationale: Names Onesimus and keeps spiritual parenthood and prison context.
verses.before: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became in my chains.
verses.after: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became while in chains.
verses.tsw_comparator: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became in my imprisonment.

verses.rationale: Preserves the name-related useful/useless wordplay.
verses.before: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
verses.after: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he is indeed useful to you and to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps involuntary return and intense bodily affection.
verses.before: I am sending him back to you—him, that is, my own heart.
verses.after: I am sending him back to you—him, that is, my own heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am sending him back to you, sending my very heart.

verses.rationale: Retains Paul's desire, expected service and incarceration.
verses.before: I wanted to keep him with me so that he might serve me on your behalf in my chains for the good news.
verses.after: I wanted to keep him with me, so that he might serve me on your behalf while I am in chains for the good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: I would have been glad to keep him with me, in order that he might serve me on your behalf during my imprisonment for the gospel,

verses.rationale: Keeps consent and coercion contrast within an unequal relationship.
verses.before: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed might not be by compulsion but willingly.
verses.after: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed would not be forced but voluntary.
verses.tsw_comparator: but I preferred to do nothing without your consent, in order that your goodness might not be by compulsion but of your own accord.

verses.rationale: Preserves cautious perhaps and passive separation.
verses.before: Perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while: so that you might have him back forever,
verses.after: Perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while, so that you might have him back forever,
verses.tsw_comparator: For this perhaps is why he was parted from you for a while, that you might have him back forever,

verses.rationale: Names enslaved status and the requested transformed relationship without inventing manumission.
verses.before: no longer as a slave but more than a slave—a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
verses.after: no longer merely as a slave but more than a slave—as a beloved brother, especially to me, and how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: no longer as a slave but more than a slave, as a beloved brother—especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps partnership as the appeal's direct basis.
verses.before: Therefore, if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would me.
verses.after: So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
verses.tsw_comparator: So if you consider me your partner, receive him as you would receive me.

verses.rationale: Preserves possible harm, debt and Paul's assumption of liability.
verses.before: If he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge that to me.
verses.after: If he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: If he has wronged you at all, or owes you anything, charge that to my account.

verses.rationale: Keeps autograph promise and the explicit counter-debt pressure.
verses.before: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me even your own self.
verses.after: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me your very self.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—to say nothing of your owing me even your own self.

verses.rationale: Preserves Onesimus-related wordplay and the repeated heart-refreshing request.
verses.before: Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
verses.after: Yes, brother, let me benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yes, brother, I want some benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps expectation, obedience language and open-ended further action.
verses.before: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
verses.after: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
verses.tsw_comparator: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.

verses.rationale: Retains prospective visit and added social accountability.
verses.before: At the same time, prepare a guest room for me, because I hope that through your prayers I will be graciously given back to you.
verses.after: At the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I am hoping that through your prayers I will be graciously given to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps name, imprisonment and Christ relation.
verses.before: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,
verses.after: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,
verses.tsw_comparator: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends greetings to you,

verses.rationale: Preserves all four names and shared role.
verses.before: as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
verses.after: as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, my coworkers.
verses.tsw_comparator: and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.

verses.rationale: Retains singular spirit addressed within a plural blessing context.
verses.before: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
verses.after: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
